sections.content:
5,210 people

were counted on the census as "importers and exporters" in England and Wales in March 2021.

This makes this type of work the eighth least common occupation reported on the census.

Importers and exporters buy commodities from overseas for the home market and sell home-produced commodities to overseas markets.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "importers and exporters" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 35 to 39 years. Of the whole working population 11.5% were aged 35 to 39 years. For people working as "importers and exporters", 12.9% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "importers and exporters" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "importers and exporters" included:

  • travel agents
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • medical and dental technicians

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

A similar number of men and women had this job

Among people working as "importers and exporters" there were a similar number of men and women (51.6% compared with 48.4%).

This means "importers and exporters" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "business and public service associate professionals".

Men made up 51.6% and women made up 48.4% of "importers and exporters"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "importers and exporters" included:

  • actors, entertainers and presenters
  • conservation professionals
  • higher education teaching professionals

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "importers and exporters" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "importers and exporters" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "importers and exporters", 7.3% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (86.2% compared with 13.8%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (89%) than self-employed (11%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Hounslow, this is in the region of London.
